purpose: Ambrisentan is used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), which is high blood pressure in the arteries that carry blood to your lungs. It helps improve your ability to exercise and slows down the worsening of the disease. It is meant for adults who have been diagnosed with this specific type of high blood pressure.
how_it_works: Your body makes a natural chemical called endothelin that can cause the blood vessels in your lungs to tighten and narrow. Ambrisentan blocks the place where endothelin attaches, which helps relax and widen those blood vessels. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood through your lungs, lowering the pressure and improving blood flow.
common_side_effects: Swelling in your hands, legs, or ankles (fluid retention) is the most common side effect. You may also notice headaches, flushing or feeling warm in your face, nasal congestion or a stuffy nose, pounding heartbeat, and feeling tired. Some people develop mild anemia (low red blood cell count).
warnings: This medication can cause serious birth defects — do not take it if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Women who can get pregnant must use two reliable forms of birth control and take monthly pregnancy tests. Do not donate blood while on this medication. Tell your doctor right away if you notice rapid weight gain or significant swelling, as this may signal fluid buildup. Regular blood tests to check your liver and blood count are important while taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg once daily if needed and if you are tolerating the medication well. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, split, or chew it.
